warnings.warning: When the drag-force term is converted to work, the printed substituted form appears to drop a required three-dimensional path-length factor; retain ds=sqrt(1+y'^2+z'^2)dx when re-deriving.
The vertical-air projection does not establish the transformation from local cross-section/downhill velocity to global vertical velocity; declare the coordinate basis before reuse.
Quadratic vector drag should project beta*|v|*v into each component; the printed scalar y equation uses beta*v_y^2 and omits coupled downhill speed.
The next-cycle ledger subtracts downhill gravitational gain and athlete work, opposite their signs in the earlier balance; rebuild one signed energy ledger before reuse.
The factor (1/3)ml^2 is an end-pivot stick inertia, but the angular-momentum reference point is not stated; do not reuse it for center-of-mass spin without correction.
The course tangent rate v/rho is treated as rider-body angular velocity without a contact torque or angular-impulse model; this is a proxy, not a closed mechanic.
Redirecting the modeled downhill kinetic energy into the vertical component requires an athlete-course impulse and feasibility bound; energy availability alone does not supply direction.
The paper calls k an increment but later normalizes it like a derivative; verify units, endpoint tangent, curvature continuity, and minimum radius in any reuse.
Theta=omega*t with omega proportional to L0 assumes fixed inertia and conflicts with the paper's own posture-dependent I(t) discussion; integrate L/I(t) instead.
The imported athlete-level score regression has unverified citation, units, population, and transfer domain; never use its optimized value as independent validation of a course.

global_organization_chain: Use the Summary to reveal the complete intellectual itinerary: two objectives, common physical base, athlete extension, numerical search, hybrid score, practice, and one explicit limit.
Define the half-pipe and judging context, then turn subjective performance into the two measurable proxies of vertical air and rotation.
Bound the repeated physical object with cycle/fly definitions, a parameter dictionary, geometric admissibility, loss laws, and baseline athlete behavior.
Decompose one cycle into contact and airborne phases; within contact move from forces to path-integrated loss, athlete work, and takeoff state.
Use the takeoff state twice: once for projectile height/distance/next-cycle energy and once for course-controlled initial angular momentum and trick interpretation.
Benchmark the analytic case against numerical output, run a local sensitivity/plausibility pass, then add athlete path, velocity, posture, and landing choices as an explicit extension.
Return to the official questions only after constructing the common model: local factor explanations first, bounded joint geometry next, flexible transition shape last.
For rotation tailoring, preserve the dependency order airtime -> initial angular momentum -> total rotation before combining the single-objective designs through predicted score.
Move from theoretical optima back to practice through radius, flat bottom, retained energy, and finite trick-count/run-length tradeoffs.
Close with a concrete capability inventory and two repeated model-does-not limitation statements rather than replacing the positive architecture with a defect list.

main_argument_chains.claim: A complete-cycle state links course geometry and rider path to vertical air, rotation, and the next cycle.
support_steps: Derive forces, normal load, path length, energy loss, and stand-up work.
Hand takeoff speed to projectile and angular-momentum branches.
Return E_reach to the following cycle and add athlete controls.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: One common mechanics chain can evaluate multiple course objectives while preserving repeated-run consequences.

main_argument_chains.claim: Vertical-air course design should proceed from interpretable factor effects to bounded joint geometry and then flexible transition shape.
support_steps: Define Vertical Air as the objective over course and path.
Plot paired responses for width, height, flat, slope, and zt with fixed defaults.
Declare the five-variable search box and selected parameter vector.
Use a convex-curve genetic representation for transition shape.
Interpret the selected shape with an ellipse-plus-vert surrogate.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The reader can distinguish why individual variables matter from how the final bounded candidate is assembled.

main_argument_chains.claim: Rotation tailoring is a dependent sequence rather than one undifferentiated objective.
support_steps: Combine angular state and airtime into total rotation.
Use the score equation to seek a compromise curve.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The hybrid result is interpretable through the component objectives it inherits, even though its empirical transfer still needs validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: A performance optimum becomes a practical course only after constructability, retained-state, and finite-run requirements are restored.
support_steps: Require a nontrivial curvature radius and operational flat bottom.
Compare vertical air against E_reach across width, height, and flat.
Translate 5-8 tricks in 110 m into a cycle-capacity condition.
State capabilities and unresolved model scope separately.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not present a single unconstrained stochastic shape as the final construction decision; report tradeoffs and missing constraints.
